requirement_text.REQ-064: Execute Decision 0006's D2: drop tenant_id from the ten schema-isolated business tables. Full text: see handoffs/WF02-REQ064-20260818/step-01-code-designer.json's requirement_text.

task.description:
Independently validate lib/letflow/design/req064-drop-tenant-id.md against REQ-064's acceptance criteria and decision 0006. Read the design artefact directly -- do not read CODE-DESIGNER's handoff result.summary as a substitute.

CODE-DESIGNER's own report flags several corrections it made to the requirement text's own claims -- verify each of these independently rather than accepting them on the design's own say-so, since a wrong correction here would be worse than the original requirement text's error:

1. **Tokens-table module ownership.** The design claims Letflow.Engine.TokenRecord (not Engine.Token) owns the tokens table and its tenant_id field, because REQ-063 renamed the schema module to avoid REQ-044's own separate Engine.Token in-memory struct. Read lib/letflow/engine/token_record.ex and lib/letflow/engine/token.ex directly yourself and confirm this is accurate -- which one actually has `use Ecto.Schema` and a tenant_id field, and which is a plain struct.

2. **Call-site count and per-site decisions.** The design claims 14 tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 call sites (not the requirement text's ~13 estimate), with two sites in definitions.ex (activate/2 and rollback_definition_version/4) explicitly left UNCHANGED because tenant_id there feeds a genuine functional consumer (a permission/service-scope checker) unrelated to the dropped column, not just column-stamping. Read those two specific call sites in lib/letflow/definitions.ex directly and confirm this distinction is real -- if it's wrong (i.e. those two sites also just discard/stamp), that's a design defect that would leave dead code or break a real feature.

3. **A third tenant_id-leading index not named in the requirement text.** The design found index(:users, [:tenant_id, :status, :inserted_at]) during a direct read of the shipped users migration, and defaults to dropping it with no replacement index, flagged as an open question. Read priv/repo/migrations/20260819000003_create_users_tenant_scoped.exs directly and confirm this index actually exists as described. Evaluate whether dropping it with no replacement is safe (does anything query users by status+inserted_at within a tenant schema? grep for it) or whether the design should have specified a replacement index -- this is exactly the kind of open question a design gate should push back on if the default (drop, no replacement) risks a real performance regression on a query path that exists.

4. **Moduledoc scope.** The design extends moduledoc updates beyond the requirement text's two named modules (Engine.Task/TokenRecord, Identity.User) to also cover Identity.Group and the three EventStore schema modules. Confirm these additional modules genuinely have tenant_id-describing prose that would go stale (spot-check at least two of them directly).

Standard procedure: for each acceptance criterion, verify a corresponding design element exists, no TBD/deferral language, function signatures fully specified with error shapes, cross-module dependencies listed, no implementation code (.ex/.exs bodies) present -- only signatures/type shapes.
acceptance_criteria: Every REQ-064 acceptance criterion has a corresponding design element, no TBD/deferral language
TokenRecord vs Token module ownership independently confirmed against the real files
The two left-unchanged definitions.ex call sites (activate/2, rollback_definition_version/4) independently confirmed to have a genuine non-stamping consumer, not just asserted
The third users index finding confirmed against the real migration file, and its drop-with-no-replacement default evaluated for safety, not rubber-stamped
Moduledoc scope extension to Identity.Group and EventStore modules spot-checked against real files
